newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up 2.10 pct at two-year high.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up 2.10 pct at two-year high.

text.p: Taiwan shares closed sharply higher on Wednesday after the island's top securities regulator said on Tuesday he was optimistic about the local stock market as the influence of non-economic factors was diminishing.
"I believe the market will have a rosy future. I am optimistic," Lu Tung-ying, chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, was quoted by an aide as saying.
The index ended 144.41 points or 2.10 percent higher at 7,019.43 points, the highest since 7,051.49 recorded on January 5, 1995.
Turnover was relatively heavy at T$79.74 billion.
Several brokers noted active buying by government-related funds, which helped boost the financial sector, and said they may have been using Lu's bullish remarks to kindle a rally.

"The government is really bullish this time, trying either through comments or actual entries to diminish the impact of recent political uncertainties," said Alex Chen, assistant research manager at HSBC James Capel Taiwan.

The market plunged 1.64 percent on Saturday after Taiwan provincial governor James Soong's shock resignation to protest moves to dismantle his largely redundant administration, but has rebounded in three consecutive sessions since Monday.

Financials led the overall upward momentum, rising 4.57 percent, with all Big Three state-run banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- rising by the daily seven percent limit to T$166, T$175 and T$136, respectively.
Brokers said sector, which is heavily weighted in the index, also rose on news that the exchange had set a plan to allow warrants on blue chip stock, a significant liberalisation.

Stock exchange officials said on Wednesday they were seeking regulatory approval for a scheme to let local and foreign banks or securities brokerages issue warrants on local blue chips having market value over T$30 billion.
